name: Complete Blood Count (CBC)
description: A fundamental diagnostic tool that evaluates the overall health of your blood, screening for a wide range of disorders including anemia, infection, and leukemia.

quickSummary.primaryPurpose: Evaluates overall health and detects a wide range of disorders, including anemia, infection, and leukemia.
quickSummary.whatItMeasures: Red blood cells, white blood cells, hemoglobin, hematocrit, and platelets.
quickSummary.preparation: No special preparation is usually required.

overview: A complete blood count (CBC) is a blood test used to evaluate your overall health and detect a wide range of disorders, including anemia, infection and leukemia.
A complete blood count test measures several components and features of your blood, including:
- Red blood cells, which carry oxygen
- White blood cells, which fight infection
- Hemoglobin, the oxygen-carrying protein in red blood cells
- Hematocrit, the proportion of red blood cells to the fluid component, or plasma, in your blood
- Platelets, which help with blood clotting

measures.name: Red Blood Cells (RBC)
measures.description: Measures the number of red blood cells, which carry oxygen from your lungs to the rest of your body.

measures.name: White Blood Cells (WBC)
measures.description: Measures the number of white blood cells, which fight infection and disease.

measures.name: Hemoglobin (Hb)
measures.description: Measures the amount of hemoglobin, the oxygen-carrying protein in red blood cells.

measures.name: Hematocrit (Hct)
measures.description: Measures the proportion of blood volume that is occupied by red blood cells.

measures.name: Platelet Count
measures.description: Measures the number of platelets, which help with blood clotting.

procedure.title: Preparation
procedure.description: You typically don't need any special preparation before a complete blood count test. You can eat and drink normally before the test.

procedure.title: Collection
procedure.description: A healthcare professional will clean the skin on your arm with an antiseptic wipe and insert a small needle into a vein to draw blood into a test tube or vial.

procedure.title: Aftercare
procedure.description: After the blood draw, pressure will be applied to the puncture site to stop any bleeding, and a small bandage will be placed over it. You can resume normal activities immediately.

interpretation.high: May indicate infection, inflammation, or dehydration.
interpretation.low: May indicate anemia, malnutrition, or bone marrow suppression.
interpretation.notes: An abnormal result doesn't always mean a disease. Your physician will look at trends over time and compare them with your symptoms.
